before.title: 12V Battery Parasitic Drain / No-Start After Sitting
before.description: GLA owners frequently report a dead 12V battery and no-start after the car sits, caused by parasitic drain. Documented contributors include a control module (e.g., signal acquisition module) failing to enter sleep mode, a relay rapidly cycling when the car is off, and 'intelligent' alternator charging strategies that under-charge a battery on short trips. On the GLA 250e/48V-equipped cars, auxiliary/12V supply faults can also cause complete power loss. The drain leaves owners stranded and can trigger cascading electrical warnings.
before.solution: Perform a parasitic draw test (current with vehicle asleep), isolate the offending circuit/module by pulling fuses, and replace the faulty relay or module that won't sleep. Verify charging-system health and replace a worn 12V battery (and the auxiliary battery where fitted), then re-register the battery via diagnostics. Latest module/software updates address some sleep-mode faults.
symptoms: Dead battery / no crank after sitting

citations.title: 12V Main Battery Drain - Mercedes-Benz GLA Forum
2018 Mercedes GLA Parasitic Battery Drain (relay constantly energizing) - JustAnswer

proposal.title: 12V Battery Parasitic Drain / No-Start After Sitting
proposal.description: Mercedes communications directly support discharged 12V starter batteries and no-start conditions on both GLA generations. Communications 10157073, 10157076, 10158199 and 10158370 cover discharged batteries, no-start complaints and excessive quiescent current on earlier GLA vehicles. Communication 10217159 identifies a later bus-keepawake path in the headlamp, ALC, instrument cluster, SAM, PTCU or ESP control units, with U116000 and a software-first remedy. Communication 11018206 warns that a discharged battery does not automatically require replacement and requires onboard-data analysis to identify the cause. These records do not establish one universal relay, charging-strategy or 48V-battery cause for every 2015-2023 GLA.
proposal.solution: Preserve the initial quick test and onboard electrical data before charging or disconnecting the battery. Measure quiescent current, identify any bus-keepawake control unit and follow its VIN-specific software or circuit path; separately test battery health after charging. Do not buy a battery, relay, SAM, headlamp module or 48V component from this page; the discharge cause and fitment must be established first.
symptoms: 12V state of charge and no-start condition documented
quiescent current or bus-keepawake path identified
battery health tested after controlled charging

before.title: 7G-DCT (724.0) Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder & Mechatronics Failure
before.description: The X156 GLA's 7G-DCT 7-speed wet dual-clutch transmission (type 724.0) is prone to low-speed shudder/judder, jerky or delayed engagement, and clutch slip, typically emerging from ~40,000-75,000 mi (60,000-120,000 km). Root causes are wet multi-plate clutch wear, degraded/contaminated DCT fluid, and failure of the mechatronics control unit that manages clutch pressures. Stop-go urban driving and skipped fluid services accelerate it. Once shuddering begins, worn clutch packs can progress to a no-drive condition within a few thousand km.
before.solution: First step is a DCT fluid (DCTF) and filter change with a STAR/XENTRY clutch adaptation reset; this often clears early shudder. Persistent slip/jerk requires clutch pack replacement, and an internal-failure mechatronics unit must be replaced and re-coded. Mercedes addressed some early cars via TCU software updates. Use only the specified DCTF and adhere to the ~40k mi adaptation/60k km fluid intervals.
symptoms: Low-speed shudder or vibration when pulling away

before.title: Diesel EGR/DPF Clogging & AdBlue (SCR) System Faults (OM651/OM654)
before.description: GLA diesels (GLA 200d/220d), popular in Germany and the EU, develop clogged EGR valves and diesel particulate filters from soot buildup, plus AdBlue/SCR (NOx reduction) faults. EGR carbon fouling causes rough idle, reduced power and emissions faults; DPF blockage triggers limp mode if regeneration can't complete (common with short urban trips). AdBlue/SCR issues include crystallization from irregular use, sensor/NOx-sensor faults, level/quality warnings and countdown-to-no-start messages. The OM651 also shares timing-chain-stretch tendencies.
before.solution: Carry out periodic motorway runs to allow active DPF regeneration; clean or replace a clogged EGR valve and clear/replace a blocked DPF. SCR faults require diagnosing and replacing NOx sensors, the SCR/AdBlue metering/dosing unit, or clearing crystallization, then resetting the no-start countdown via XENTRY. Use only fresh, correct-spec AdBlue and keep the tank topped.
symptoms: Check engine and DPF warning lights
AdBlue level/quality warning with no-start countdown

before.title: M270/M274 Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Wear (Cold-Start Rattle)
before.description: The GLA's M270/M274 turbo four-cylinder petrol engines are widely documented to suffer timing chain elongation and tensioner/guide wear, usually presenting between roughly 40,000-80,000 mi. A loose chain produces a distinctive rattle for the first few seconds after a cold start until oil pressure loads the tensioner. A related defect is the camshaft tone/reluctor ring slipping, throwing timing-correlation faults. Left unaddressed, a stretched chain can jump time and cause valve-to-piston contact and major engine damage.
before.solution: Confirm with live cam/crank correlation data; replace the timing chain, tensioner, and guides as a set (and the camshaft sprockets/tone ring if the ring has slipped). Strict adherence to short oil-change intervals with correct-spec oil slows wear. German specialists recommend chain inspection/replacement around 100,000-150,000 km on these engines.

before.title: MBUX/COMAND Infotainment Black Screen & Reboot (NHTSA Recall 21V354)
before.description: GLA infotainment units suffer black/frozen screens and spontaneous reboots. On H247 cars this is the NVIDIA-Tegra-based MBUX head unit, which can fail to boot or reboot ~50 seconds after startup, disabling the rearview camera image (the basis of NHTSA recall 21V354 covering 2019-2021 MB models including the GLA). On X156 cars the COMAND/Audio 20 system has analogous software bugs. Because climate control runs through the touchscreen on H247, a frozen screen also locks out HVAC. Weak 12V battery voltage dips and heat aggravate it.
before.solution: For the recall, dealers apply an over-the-air or in-shop MBUX software update at no cost; verify the 21V354 remedy was performed. General fixes include the latest head-unit software, ensuring a healthy 12V battery, and head-unit replacement if hardware (Tegra chip) has failed. X156 COMAND issues are typically resolved by software updates.

before.title: Rear Differential Carrier Whine/Clunk on 4MATIC Models
before.description: On 4MATIC GLA250/GLA220d cars the rear differential carrier assembly is a documented weak point, producing whine, growl, or clunk from the rear (especially on/off throttle and cornering), often at surprisingly low mileage (~50,000-70,000 mi). The differential uses a very small fluid volume (under ~1 liter) that breaks down and contaminates; some units also had marginal bearings. This is distinct from the transfer-case/PTU noise and originates in the rear axle carrier itself. A neglected unit can develop heavy bearing/gear wear.
before.solution: Diagnose by rear diff fluid condition first; an early fluid change often quiets humming/popping and is cheap insurance. Worn bearings or gear noise require rebuilding or replacing the rear differential carrier assembly. Establish a periodic rear-diff fluid service interval rather than relying on factory 'lifetime' fill.
symptoms: Whine or growl from rear that changes with speed
Clunk when coming to a stop or cornering

before.title: Water Pump Failure
before.description: The electric water pump on the M270 engine fails, causing loss of coolant circulation and rapid overheating. The pump motor or impeller breaks, and failure is often sudden with no warning. Common between 50,000-90,000 miles.
before.solution: Replace the electric water pump and thermostat together. Use OEM or Pierburg (OEM supplier) parts. Flush the cooling system with fresh Mercedes-approved coolant. Monitor the temperature gauge closely on high-mileage GLA models.

communityRecommendations.content: If the temperature gauge moves above the halfway mark, pull over immediately. The electric water pump gives zero warning before complete failure — overheating for even 2 minutes can warp the head.

proposal.title: Water Pump Failure
proposal.description: The reviewed GLA manufacturer-communication and recall corpus does not establish a 2015-2020 M270 water-pump-failure identity. Exact cooling records found in the model inventory concern a generic 2020 coolant-line leak or later M139 thermostat/debris procedures, not the frozen GLA250 M270 water pump. No primary record supports the stored bearing/seal mechanism, overheating progression, 45,000-80,000-mile range, replacement ladder, repair price or 800-owner count.
proposal.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system, inspect for external leakage and verify coolant circulation, thermostat control, fan operation and temperature-sensor data before condemning the pump. Confirm the exact engine and VIN in Mercedes workshop and parts systems. Do not buy a water pump, thermostat, belt, tensioner or coolant kit from this page; the failed component and fitment are not established.
symptoms: coolant loss and leak location documented
pump, thermostat, fan and sensor paths separated
